expectation: I expect the messenger RNA to be placed at the ribosome, ready for protein assembly.

expectation: I expect a chain of amino acids corresponding to the glucose transporter gene, possibly needing further folding.

effect: The ribosome made a glucose transporter chain, which now appears ready for folding and targeting.
reaction: The result follows the expected protein-building sequence.
reason: The only offered combination should prepare the chain to function as a transporter.
expectation: I expect the chain to fold into a glucose transporter and be directed toward the cell membrane.

effect: The transporter chain is folded and in a membrane vesicle, ready to be combined with the cell boundary.
reaction: The vesicle suggests how the transporter reaches the membrane, though the result gives little explanation.
reason: The only offered combination should add the transporter to the cell boundary and advance the fuel-admission goal.
expectation: I expect the transporter to be incorporated into the membrane so glucose can enter the cell.

effect: The vesicle inserted the transporter into the membrane, completing the fuel-admission goal and the chapter.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the protein-making sequence connect back to the cell boundary.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the transporter was most worthwhile because it connected the gene-to-protein sequence to a visible change in what can cross the cell boundary.

leastWorthwhile.text: The separate placement steps felt procedural, especially when the next combination was immediately apparent.

surprise.text: The RNA result clarified how a working copy reaches the ribosome while the DNA stays in the nucleus.

arbitrary.text: No action felt wholly arbitrary, though the pump's purpose was not clearly explained when it was fitted.

continue.text: I would be mildly interested in continuing to see how the working cell connects to tissues and body systems, though I would hope for more meaningful choices and explanations.
